name: Hydra
title: Holidays in Hydra
intro: A car-free Greek island of stone mansions around a horseshoe harbour, where donkeys carry the luggage, two hours from Athens by ferry. Here's what Hydra is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Stone houses and a bell tower around Hydra's harbour
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are best, warm with calm seas and quieter lanes. July and August are hot and busy with day-trippers and yachts. Winter is quiet, with many places closed.

things.name: Hydra harbour
things.blurb: Cafés and stone mansions around the old port, watching boats and donkeys.

things.name: Swim off the rocks
things.blurb: Swim from the platforms at Spilia and Hydronetta, just west of the harbour.

things.name: Coastal walk to Kamini
things.blurb: An easy path to a fishing village with a tavern by the water.

things.name: Water taxi to Bisti
things.blurb: Pine-backed coves on the far side of the island.

things.name: Historical Archives Museum
things.blurb: Island history and its role in the Greek War of Independence.

things.name: Monastery walk
things.blurb: Climb to the Profitis Ilias monastery for big views.

faqs.question: Is Hydra worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. With no cars, it's peaceful and beautiful, and an easy escape from Athens.

faqs.question: How do you get to Hydra?
faqs.answer: Fly into Athens, then take a fast ferry from Piraeus, about 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours.

faqs.question: Can you do Hydra as a day trip from Athens?
faqs.answer: Yes, but staying a night or two is much better, when the day-trippers have gone.

faqs.question: Does Hydra have beaches?
faqs.answer: Mostly rocks and small pebble coves, reached on foot or by water taxi.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Hydra?
faqs.answer: May, June, September and October, around 23 to 29°C.
